verdicts.note: Claude sits on the sprocket's bright brass hub at the teeth-circle center; codex is ~36px left of center on the inner web.

The lower chain sprocket is genuinely visible on the crank arm; claude marked it but placed the dot on the crank-axle hex bolt ~50px below the actual sprocket teeth-circle center, while codex omitted it.
The near cylinder gear's end-flange axis is the white shaft bolt in the black bearing bracket; claude is on it, codex is ~50px left on the brass face.

Codex's low-confidence point lands on helical-drum body texture that most likely belongs to the same drum as gear_1 (its rear body) rather than a distinct second gear whose center is resolvable; claude's occluded call is the safer read.
Both agree the conical stack is occluded behind the crank pedestal / cylinder drum in this front view — correct.
Both agree the rocker-arm fan is behind the platen / edge-on and unresolvable from the front — correct.
Both mark the same top-left outer corner of the green top casting within ~8px; both good, no left/right mirroring.
Claude is exactly on the outer top-right corner of the green casting; codex is ~46px left, sitting on the top face near the silver rail base rather than the outer corner.
Claude sits at the true bottom-left corner of the green base slab; codex (y=3655) floats in the black background well above-left of the slab — the systematic 'higher edge' error.
Claude is at the true bottom-right corner of the green base slab; codex (y=3651) is ~100px too high, placed on the slab face rather than the bottom corner.
Both correctly record all four rear top/base corners as occluded in the front view.

summary: Claude was clearly more accurate on this image, winning the pinion, cylinder_gear_1, top-right corner, and both base corners, while tying the (agreed) occlusions and the top-left corner. Codex has a systematic base-corner error: it marked both bottom corners ~100px too high (base_front_left actually landing in the black background off the slab), matching the known 'higher edge' dispute — claude correctly hit the true bottom outer corners. Both attempts use a consistent, non-mirrored machine-relative naming (image-left = machine left, crank side = right); the only point where codex arguably added value was attempting cylinder_gear_center_2, but that point sits on ambiguous helical-drum texture likely belonging to gear_1, so claude's occluded call is defensible.
